app.name: HubSpot CRM app (via HubSpot Developer Platform)

verdict.summary: Creating your own HubSpot app and connecting your own test account is quick and free. Installs beyond your own accounts are capped until you sign the Acceptable Use Policy, and a public Marketplace listing needs a manual HubSpot review plus platform migrations whose deadlines fall within days of today (Oct 31 and Nov 2, 2026).
verdict.hands_on_effort: Test setup about 1-3 hours (estimate, not from sources). Listing prep and migration: several days of work (estimate).
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Under an hour once the developer account exists (estimate, not from sources).
verdict.approval_wait: None for testing and private installs. Marketplace listing: HubSpot states an initial review within 10 business days; third-party sites report 3-8 weeks (unofficial).

gates.name: Development / developer test account
gates.unlocks: Create the app in the HubSpot Developer Platform, set a redirect URL, and connect your own account. Until the Acceptable Use Policy is signed, installs are limited to developer test accounts, which must be separate accounts inside your developer account.
limits: Free HubSpot developer-account sign-up; no login wall on the portal (community/probed).
A developer account cannot host the install itself; you need a separate test account inside it.
Unverified apps show a warning banner, and the installer must type a confirmation phrase to proceed.

gates.name: Privately distributed (allowlisted accounts)
gates.unlocks: After you sign the Acceptable Use Policy in the Distribution tab, a private OAuth app can be installed in up to 10 allowlisted accounts (excluding developer test accounts). Users need the install permissions described in the scope notes.
limits: Up to 10 allowlisted accounts for private OAuth distribution.
Solution Partners reportedly get up to 100 (community announcement, not on HubSpot's docs page).
A marketplace-bound app that is not yet listed is capped at 25 installs.
Only one verified domain per developer account, shared by all apps in it; verification usually completes within an hour, DNS up to 48 hours.
Token lifetimes not captured in findings.
gates.time_to_reach: Same day once the developer account is set up (no review mentioned in the sources)

gates.name: Marketplace listing (public)
gates.unlocks: Public install for any HubSpot account through a Marketplace listing reviewed by HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team.
limits: Manual review by the Ecosystem Quality team; submissions that miss published criteria are rejected.
Only one app can be under review at a time; a second submission is rejected automatically.
Requires at least three active, unique, non-affiliated production installs with successful activity in the past 30 days.
OAuth must be the only authorization method.
Sensitive and highly sensitive data scopes need separate access from the Ecosystem Quality team.
gates.time_to_reach: HubSpot states an initial review within 10 business days; full review and feedback capped at about 60 days from when feedback is shared. Third-party sites report 3-8 weeks for a first listing (unofficial).

steps.title: Check your deadlines and current app status first
steps.detail: Today is Oct 28, 2026. Classic CRM cards are fully deprecated on Oct 31, 2026, and new listings must run platform v2025.2 or v2026.03 from Nov 2, 2026. If you already have a public app, check whether it is a legacy app created before June 23, 2026 (see blockers).
gotchas: Other sources conflict on the legacy creation cutoff date (May 26 vs. June 23, 2026). Use HubSpot's changelog.

steps.title: Create a free HubSpot developer account and a test account
steps.detail: Sign up for a HubSpot developer account at developers.hubspot.com. Inside that developer account, create a separate test account; you will install the app there, because the developer account cannot host the install itself.

steps.title: Create the app in the Developer Platform
steps.detail: Create a new app (project) in your developer account. The exact app-creation click path was not verified; follow HubSpot's current create-app page. Name it so testers recognize it.
gotchas: The create-app page could not be fetched during research; confirm the menu path in your console.

steps.title: Define scopes in app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: Edit the auth block of app-hsmeta.json. Put scopes in requiredScopes, optionalScopes, or conditionallyRequiredScopes. Start from the scopes you actually use, not Composio's default list. Each app needs at least one scope.
gotchas: Unused scopes must be removed before listing.
Optional scopes are dropped from the authorization request if the account lacks the matching tool; read the token to see what was granted.

steps.title: Set the Redirect URI on the Auth tab
steps.detail: In the project's Auth tab, add the redirect URL and make sure it matches exactly what you register. Production URLs must use https with a domain name, not an IP.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Localhost http is allowed only for local testing.
The value must match the redirect URL registered on the Auth tab exactly.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID and Client secret from the Client credentials section of the Auth tab. Enter them in your Composio auth config for HubSpot as custom OAuth credentials. The secret can be rotated from the same tab.

steps.title: Ensure every required scope is in the authorization URL
steps.detail: Check that every scope marked required in the Auth settings appears in the scope parameter of the authorization URL. A missing required scope makes the authorization page show an error. Code exchange uses client_id, client_secret, and grant_type=authorization_code; PKCE is not mentioned in HubSpot's docs.

steps.title: Upload the app configuration
steps.detail: Run the hs project upload command from the project folder to push your app-hsmeta.json changes to your account. Scope changes take effect on upload.

steps.title: Run a test install in your test account
steps.detail: Connect the app from Composio using your test account. Expect the unverified-app warning banner and the confirmation phrase. Check Development, Monitoring, Logs, OAuth tab in HubSpot for the authorization request, grant, and token exchange.
gotchas: Confirm the installing user has the permissions required for each scope (see scope notes).

steps.title: Sign the Acceptable Use Policy and add allowlisted accounts
steps.detail: In the Distribution tab, begin publishing and sign HubSpot's Acceptable Use Policy. Then add up to 10 allowlisted accounts for private installs. Optionally add one verified domain via a DNS TXT record in the developer account; it applies to all apps in that account.
gotchas: Until the AUP is signed, installs are limited to developer test accounts.
Only one verified domain per developer account.

steps.title: Draft listing documents and demo
steps.detail: Draft the Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, an integration-specific public setup guide, shared-data documentation that matches your scopes, and support resources. Record a demo video or guided walkthrough of core flows and permission use. Put the Terms and Privacy URLs live first.
gotchas: Pricing on the listing must match your website.
Listing needs at least one support contact method.
Login test credentials are no longer required; the demo video replaces them.

steps.title: Meet installs and agreement requirements
steps.detail: Get at least three active, unique production installs that are not affiliated with your organization and show successful activity in the last 30 days. Confirm OAuth is the only authorization method. Review and agree to the Technology Partner Program Agreement.
gotchas: Apps serving only restricted industries and apps using classic CRM cards cannot be listed.

steps.title: Migrate the app to supported architecture
steps.detail: Move the app to platform v2025.2 or v2026.03. Replace classic CRM cards with app cards. Add a call to the Uninstall App endpoint and switch token code exchange to the OAuth v3 endpoint (POST /oauth/2026-03/token). Complete the security questionnaire on OAuth token storage and access.
gotchas: Composio's token URL (api.hubapi.com/oauth/v1/token) may not match the v3 endpoint required for certification. Confirm before submitting.

steps.title: Submit the listing for review
steps.detail: Submit the app for Marketplace listing. Only one app can be under review at a time, so do not submit a second app while one is pending.
gotchas: Sensitive-data scopes must be approved by HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team before publication.

steps.title: Wait for HubSpot's review
steps.detail: HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team reviews by hand and states an initial review within 10 business days. Full review and feedback can take up to about 60 days. Respond to feedback promptly.
steps.est_time: 10 business days initial; up to about 60 days full review

requirements.detail: Sign up at developers.hubspot.com. The portal loads without a login wall.
Install needs a test account inside your developer account; the developer account cannot host the install.
Production redirect must use https with a domain name; http only for localhost.
Required before installs outside developer test accounts.
Cap for privately distributed OAuth apps; 25-install cap for unlisted marketplace-bound apps.

requirements.item: Live Terms and Privacy Policy URLs
requirements.detail: Must be live and up to date for listing.

requirements.item: Public integration setup guide, shared-data docs, support contact
requirements.detail: Listing needs a public setup guide, shared-data documentation matching requested scopes, live support resources, and at least one support contact method.
Replaces test login credentials since March 31, 2026.
Successful activity in the past 30 days; OAuth must be the only authorization method.
Must review and agree before listing.
v2025.2 or v2026.03 for new listings from Nov 2, 2026.

requirements.item: No classic CRM cards; app cards only
Uninstall App endpoint and OAuth v3 token endpoint
requirements.detail: Required for new certification and recertification submissions.

requirements.item: Security questionnaire on OAuth token access and storage
requirements.detail: Covers encryption, access controls, token lifecycle.

requirements.item: Enterprise subscription on installing account for sensitive data
requirements.detail: Only for sensitive-data scopes; a super admin completes re-authorization.

scopes.scope: Composio default list (about 37 scopes, e.g. crm.objects.contacts.read, crm.objects.deals.write)
scopes.effect: Listed apps must use every scope they request. Request only what your agent uses, and make subset-only scopes optional or conditionally required. Tiers for individual scopes were not classified in the findings.
Installing users need the matching Import permission group in addition to the HubSpot Marketplace access permission for standard-account installs.

scopes.scope: Sensitive per-object scopes (contacts, companies, deals, appointments, custom objects, projects, tickets)
scopes.effect: Must request access from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team; allowlisted for testing before publication, then users must re-authorize. Requires Enterprise subscription on the installing account.
Need additional scopes beyond the sensitive family and are review-gated. Listed apps must not request sensitive scopes through app cards.
Dropped from the authorization request when the account lacks the matching tool; read the token to see what was granted.

blockers.cause: A legacy unlisted public app has more installs than the private cap allows.
blockers.fix: No clear exemption path found in community reports. Reduce installs or move the app to Projects with HubSpot support; the source gives no contact channel.

blockers.symptom: Public app created before June 23, 2026 is on legacy architecture
blockers.cause: HubSpot's changelog says these apps move to unsupported status on September 15, with enforcement in September 2027. That September 15 date is already past as of 2026-10-28.
blockers.fix: Check your app's status now. Migrate to Projects to keep it listed. Confirm current status with HubSpot before planning a listing.

blockers.symptom: Listing rejected: classic CRM cards or unsupported platform version
blockers.cause: Classic CRM cards are fully deprecated Oct 31, 2026; new listings must use v2025.2 or v2026.03 from Nov 2, 2026.
blockers.fix: Move to app cards and a supported platform version before submitting.

blockers.symptom: Sensitive-data scope request blocked or unusable
blockers.cause: Sensitive scopes need Ecosystem Quality approval and an Enterprise subscription on the installing account; app cards cannot use them.
blockers.fix: Request sensitive-scope access early, or drop those scopes if you do not need them.

blockers.cause: A scope marked required in Auth settings is missing from the authorization URL scope parameter.
blockers.fix: Add every required scope to the scope parameter of the authorization URL.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed OAuth for testing; it is the fast path. Register your own HubSpot app when you need your own client ID and redirect URL, a Marketplace listing, or sensitive scopes (these need Ecosystem Quality approval). Composio's default list is long and includes scopes listed apps must justify, so request only what you use. Verify Composio's token endpoint before listing.

open_questions: The create-an-app page and the certification-requirements page could not be fetched. The exact app-creation click path and the certification checklist are unverified.
Access and refresh token lifetimes were not captured.
The six-month listing and 60-install certified-program rule comes only from a third-party blog and is not on HubSpot's listing page.
Composio's token URL (api.hubapi.com/oauth/v1/token) differs from the OAuth v3 / 2026-03 endpoint HubSpot requires for certification. Confirm which endpoint Composio uses before submitting.
Developer-account prerequisites beyond the free sign-up (paid plan, partner enrollment, business verification) were not confirmed.
Legacy public app shutoff: a third-party aggregator says May 26, 2026; HubSpot's changelog uses June 23, 2026. Use HubSpot's changelog, and confirm the current status of any legacy app.
Current first-listing review times were not confirmed by a 2026 HubSpot entry; the 10-business-day figure is HubSpot's own initial-review statement.
The Solution Partner limit of 100 installs comes from a community post only.
